title: Why Incomplete Tasks Haunt Your Mind More Than Finished Ones
hook: Your brain actually remembers unfinished chores better than completed ones.

narration.text: Your brain actually remembers unfinished chores better than completed ones.
This is called the Zeigarnik effect, named after a Russian psychologist.
When you start a task, your mind creates a tension system for it.
This tension remains active, keeping the task in your memory, until it is completed.
Once finished, that mental tension is released, and your brain can let go.
This is why an interrupted project might stay on your mind all day.
It explains why cliffhangers are so effective in films and TV shows.
Have you noticed this mental persistence with your own to-do list?

description: Ever wonder why incomplete tasks stick in your mind more than finished ones? It is a fascinating psychological phenomenon called the Zeigarnik effect. Discover how your brain's unique memory system works.
topic: Why you often remember incomplete tasks better than completed ones, explaining the Zeigarnik effect.
